title: The Fifth — exploratory-world figure (Olympus v0.1)
description: One figure in an exploratory world (first world: Greek Olympus). A figure is a STORY DOORWAY, never a human category. Three layers are kept apart on purpose: (1) source_supported = what ancient sources actually say, with references and evidence status; (2) fifth_interpretation = what The Fifth reads in those stories (situations, tensions, expressions, questions, reveal material) — always marked as interpretation; (3) ux_story = user-facing material derived from layers 1–2 (orientation, story doors). Nothing in layer 3 may exist without a traceable origin in layer 1 via layer 2. Worlds are not required to have 12 figures.

world_id.description: Which exploratory world this figure belongs to, e.g. 'greek_olympus'.

one_sentence_intro.description: One accessible Turkish sentence for someone who knows nothing. Must not tell the user who they are.

status.description: Olympus-specific: whether ancient lists count this figure among the Twelve. Other worlds define their own membership vocabulary via 'note'.

source_supported.description: LAYER 1 — SOURCE-SUPPORTED MYTHOLOGY. Only claims that can be tied to a named ancient source or a named scholarly consensus.

variants.description: Known contradictory or alternative versions. Keep variants as variants; do not merge.

notes.description: Where the record leans on late, Roman, Orphic or popular material; where sources contradict.

fifth_interpretation.description: LAYER 2 — FIFTH INTERPRETATION. What The Fifth reads in the stories. Every item must point back to a myth_id. Polarity is NOT required: a tension may be a single open question. Never a personality claim.

statement.description: The tension in one sentence. If it is 'X ile Y arasında', say so; if it is an open question with no clean opposite, say that instead.

shape.description: between_two = genuine polarity; gradient = same thing in different doses; open_question = no clean opposite exists; sequence = one thing turning into another over time.

cost_borne_by.description: Myths often put the cost on OTHERS, not the figure. Record honestly; do not invent a self-cost to balance the record.

question.description: When does X become Y? — written in Turkish, usable as-is in a Fifth Reveal.
Turkish. Must satisfy Routing Rule v0.1 gate Q2–Q4: low-effort fact / observable event / own action / simple counterfactual the user knows; not already in the story; 2–4 one-line options.

discriminates.description: Which two readings the answer separates.

distinction.description: Portable one-line 'X ile Y arasında' form, Turkish.

fragment.description: A reusable Turkish sentence for a Reveal. Must keep uncertainty; no diagnosis; no advice.

level.description: grounded = reading follows directly from repeated myth episodes; plausible = defensible but selective; speculative = mostly modern projection, keep flagged.

ux_story.description: LAYER 3 — UX / STORY IDEA. Everything the user might see. Derived only from layers 1–2.

know_nothing_hint.description: Turkish, max ~2 sentences: what a total newcomer needs before choosing to enter this door.

visual_motifs.description: Source-attested attributes only (for a future 3D scene), e.g. 'thunderbolt', 'owl', 'trident'.

text_tr.description: Second person, present tense, a situation the user could recognise without knowing the myth. Never 'sen ... gibisin'.

perspective.description: Whose position the door puts the user in. Doors from the position of a perpetrator of violence are not written; see warnings.

overinterpretation_warnings.description: What this record must NOT be used to say. Applies to writers, the model, and the UI.

shortLabel.description: 3–6 Turkish words. Orientation for someone who knows nothing. Names a STORY TERRITORY, not a person type.

confidence.description: attested_archaic_classical = Homer, Hesiod, Homeric Hymns, lyric, tragedy, Herodotus, Plato; attested_hellenistic_roman = Callimachus, Apollodorus, Ovid, Pausanias, Hyginus; attested_late_or_orphic = Nonnus, Orphic fragments, Apuleius; scholarly_inference = consensus reconstruction (e.g., from cult/epigraphy); unsourced_popular = widely repeated, no ancient source found — keep visible, do not build on it.
